walkthroughs.body_html:
The Challenge of Resource Management — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The Challenge of Resource Management brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The Challenge of Resource Management.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between mitigation and adaptation to climate change?
options: Mitigation is done by HICs and adaptation is done by LICs.
Mitigation and adaptation mean the same thing — both are about stopping climate change.
Mitigation reduces the causes (cutting greenhouse gas emissions); adaptation reduces the impacts (e.g. building sea walls, drought-resistant crops, early warning systems).
Stratified sampling means picking samples from different strata of rock.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between random, stratified and systematic sampling?
options: Random: every member has equal chance of selection. Systematic: pick every nth item. Stratified: divide the population into groups and sample proportionally from each — ensures subgroup representation.
Stratified sampling means picking samples from different strata of rock.
All three sampling methods produce the same results.
Coral bleaching is when boats spill chemicals that whiten the reef.

When stressed (usually by warming), corals expel their symbiotic zooxanthellae (algae that provide colour and food), turning white. They can recover if stress eases, but die if it persists.
Coral bleaching is when coral is killed by sunlight bleaching its colour.
